\[
I_{\text{out}}(x,y) = \frac{1}{s} \sum_{j} \sum_{i} K(i,j)\, I(x+i,\, y+j),
\qquad
s =
\begin{cases}
\sum_{j} \sum_{i} K(i,j) & \text{if normalize is on and the sum is not } 0 \\
1 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(I\): Input channel value
- \(I_{\text{out}}\): Output channel value before the output mapping
- \(K(i,j)\): The typed weight at offset (i, j) from the center cell
- \(s\): The divisor: the sum of the weights, or 1

The offsets i and j run over the kernel with its center cell at 0. Each output value is the weighted sum of the window under the kernel. Dividing by the sum s keeps flat areas at their value. The result can be negative for kernels with negative weights, and the output mapping decides how it is shown.
